This character is told "I think this tale would win my daughter too" after explaining how he wooed his wife with stories of "battles, sieges, fortunes." This character's final words confess his desire to "die upon a kiss," and he extinguishes a candle after telling himself to "Put out the light, and then put out the light." Another character refers to this man as "making the beast with two backs." This man's ensign confesses that he refuses to "wear my heart upon my sleeve. This character, who replaces Montano as the governor of Cyprus, is infamously warned to beware the "green-eyed monster" of jealousy. He marries the daughter of Brabanzio. FTP, name this commander of Cassio, a Shakespearian protagonist who's goaded by Iago into killing his wife Desdamona.

Allied Services_ before it is read) Old Crowe helps one character in this novel operate a Ouija board that gives her the word PHIL. One character leaves a message for his wife in a recording booth that says "God damn you, you little bitch, why can't you go back home for ever and let me be?" After betraying Kite to Colleoni, one character gets a job with the Daily Messenger hiding cards for a contest under the pseudonym Kolley Kibber. The antagonist of this work tries to destroy the only evidence linking him to the murder of Fred Hale by proposing a suicide pact with the waitress Rose, but the arrival of Ida Arnold prompts him to accidentally throw acid in his own face and jump off a cliff. FTP, name this novel about Pinkie Brown and his gang in the title British seaside town, a work by Graham Greene.

A collection by Rhys Hughes which includes "Ignoble Notes" and an "Unwise Appendix" was inspired by a work by this author whose characters include a man whose worship in his hometown was spurred by the spectacle of a blinded leopard. That man is later revealed to be leprous in this author's story "Hakim, the Masked Dyer of Merv," which appears in the collection A Universal History of Infamy. The title character of another of this man's stories is a French Symbolist whose writings include the ninth and thirty- eighth chapters of the first part of the title Cervantes work. Name this author of "Pierre Menard, Author of the Quixote," a blind Argentinian.

This work's third and second stanzas describe a "moping owl" that complains to the moon and a beetle that "wheels his droning flight." Its fifteenth stanza makes a reference to John Hampden, as well as a "Cromwell guiltless of his country's blood." The last section of this work describes a character who "gave to Misery all he had, a tear." Earlier, the speaker sees a plowman who "homeward plods his weary way, / And leaves the world to darkness and to me." name this work that teaches "the paths of glory lead but to the grave" and opens as "The curfew tolls the knell of parting day," an exemplar of graveyard poetry by Thomas Gray.
Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard

Chapter five of this book details a main character who nearly goes west with an alligator. One of the characters in this book is attempting to improve his "schlemihlhood" and that same character is friends with the artist Slab, a catatonic expressionist. The titular character of this work first appears in Cairo during her youth, and then later as a Manichean priest. The second chapter of this book introduces the reader to "The Whole Sick Crew." name this novel that details the the adventures of Benny Profane's gang, as well as the relationship between the mysterious title character and the Stencil family, a work of Thomas Pynchon.

In one of this man's works, a man claiming to be a socialite plans to transcribe all of Roman history into limerick form, though he's actually helping La Grance and Croisy playing a prank on the title figures, while another work has Leandre helped by the title valet. Besides The Precious Damsels and The Schemings of Scapin, this man wrote a work where Enrique arranges Oronte's marriage to Agnes, while another of his works sees horses fed straw by Harpagon. In another of his plays, Madame Pernelle and her son Orgon interact with the purportedly pious title character. Identify this author of The Miser and Tartuffe, a noted French playwright.

In one of this man's plays, the protagonist argues with Omange and has an affair with Jane, though he is married to Thoni. Besides writing a series of one act plays including This Time, he wrote of the farmers Samuel Ndugire and Ahab Kioi in a play in which Gathoni is impregnated and disowned by her father Kiguunda. This playwright of I Will Marry When I Want told of Ilmorog bar owner Abdullah, the town where Wanja is rejected by Munira, in Petals of Blood. In another novel, he wrote of Karanja, who competes for the hand of Mumbi, though she married Gikonyo. Name this Kenyan author of A Grain of Wheat.

One character in this work disguises herself as the Queen of Fairies in order to con a character who is later blindfolded and gagged with gingerbread. One character is disguised as a Spanish Don, who takes a walk with the sister of Young Kastril. One character's goods are contracted for purchase by Ananias of Amsterdam and Tribulation Wholesome, while the Spaniard is in fact Pertinax Surly, friend of Sir Epicure Mammon. Abel Drugger loses his wife, Dame Pliant, to Face, but Face gives her up to his master Lovewit to save his own hide, though Dol Common and Subtle are not so lucky. Focusing on a fake philosopher's stone, name this Ben Jonson drama.

In a 2008 TV movie, this character was played by Olivia Williams and consoles her niece, whose suitor John Plumptree marries someone else. In another film, she speaks in sign language to her brother George, and James McAvoy plays this character's beau. In that 2007 film, this character is disgusted by the weak Wisley, has a father portrayed by James Cromwell, and is herself played by Anne Hathaway. Maggie Grace, Maria Bello, and Amy Brenneman played some of the people who formed a "club" named for this woman in another 2007 movie. Name this fictionalized writer, whose actual work was adapted by Gurinder Chadha as 2004's Bride and Prejudice.

This work's title character commits suicide after receiving a telegram which says "Safe Brindisi. Having a rattling good time." One character marries Rodney Bayham, while another ends up nurse to a woman who can only say a Latin phrase and "shuttlecocks". Maisie Maidan is the only character with a real heart defect, and the narrator's wife keeps a fake vial of heart medicine, which is in fact prussic acid. Nancy Rufford is the title figure's last affair after he tires with Florence, the narrator's wife, and his marriage to Leonora fails miserably. Name this "saddest story," told by John Dowell about Edward Ashburnham and written by Ford Maddox Ford.

This man responded to Richard Simon's Biblical criticism in his anti-deist work Religio Laici, and his play about Torrismond finding out that he is the son of Sancho, not Raymond, is called The Spanish Friar. Despite earlier declaring his love for Doralice, Palamede marries Melantha in one of this man's plays. Ventidius thwarts the schemes of Alexas in this man's play about Antony and Cleopatra, All for Love, while he satirized the Duke of Monmouth and Earl of Shaftesbury as the title characters of his roman a clef Absalom and Achitophel. Name this Restoration playwright who attacked a rival as the "monarch of dullness" in Mac Flecknoe.

One central character of this novel visits his mother in this hospital only to find his rival ill with typhoid, and reconciles that rival with his estranged wife out of pity. That character in this novel works in a stocking mill in his youth, and meets a romantic partner while vacationing at age sixteen. One character in this work is the husband of a neglectful coal miner named Walter, while another character marries Lily before dying young. The protagonist gives his mother an overdose of morphine to end her suffering from cancer and spends the novel drifting between Clara Dawes and Miriam Leivers. Name this novel about Gertrude and Paul Morel, by D.H. Lawrence.

The protagonist drops off his son to work at a gas station and finds the women of the neighborhood wasting money on a fortune teller, after hearing a speaker lament both unemployment and the dole as unmanly. Based on a novel of the same name by Luigi Bartolini, its protagonist, the father of Bruno, obtains the title object after his wife pawns her wedding sheets for money. In desparation, knowing he is about to lose his job as a poster-hanger, Antonio himself becomes the title type of person but is quickly caught by a mob. Name this film using no professional actors and directed by Vittorio De Sica, a neo-realist look at postwar Italy centering on a two- wheeled vehicle.

This book begins with an incident in which a man's thumbs and big toes are cut off, and another violent incident occurs when thousands of people are killed for mispronouncing the word "sibboleth." This book ends with a story where the Benjamites grab dancing girls and make them their wives. Villains in this book include Micah, who steals from his mother and pays a Levite to be his priest, and Abimelech, whose father defeated the Midianites using trumpets. A recurring sentence in this book states that "in those days, Israel had no king; everyone did as he saw fit," which summarizes the decadence of this period that necessitated heroes to save Israel. Identify this biblical book that tells the stories of such heroes as Deborah, Gideon, and Samson.

This man, the recipient of the ambassador Megasthenes, had his rise to power described in the play The Signet of the Minister. The tract Arthashatra was composed by his advisor Chanakya, and some stories claim that late in his life this man abdicated to follow the Jain sage Bhadrabahu. This man consolidated his power by defeating such Alexandrian satraps as Eudemus and Peithon, which allowed him to vanquish the armies of Bhadrasala and besiege Kusumapura, thus conquering the Nanda Empire, after which he won the eastern territories of Seleucus Nicator. Identify this father of Bindusara and grandfather of Ashoka, who became the first emperor of the Maurya dynasty.

This author looked back on his childhood, which included his grandfather being executed for bribery, in Dawn Blossoms Plucked at Dusk, and one of his political essays laments "a place where anything from moving a table to refitting a stove will almost always end in bloodshed." The title character of one of his stories is punished for teasing a nun in the street and despises the Imitation Foreign Devil, while another of his works uses cannibalism as a metaphor for his country's political culture. Name this Chinese author who used a discussion of Ibsen to address political change in "After Nora Walks Out, What Then?" and also wrote "The True Story of Ah Q" and a work that shares its name with a Gogol story, "Diary of a Madman."

One Nobel Laureate from this country wrote "Tales of Mystery" and "Turning Point," while another one wrote The Sovereign Sun and The Axion Esti. One author from this country wrote a poem that shares its name with a J.M. Coetzee work, "Waiting For the Barbarians." The best known author from this country wrote Freedom or Death, and The Fraticides, in addition to a novel that features Madame Hortense, name this European country home to George Seferis, Odysseus Elytis, and Constantine Cavafy, as well as the author of Toda Raba and The Last Temptation of Christ, Nikos Kazantzakis.

His short stories include works like "The Miraculous Revenge", and his novels include The Irrational Knot and Immaturity, his first.. Some minor characters in his better-known plays include Sergius Saranoff, Vivie Warren, and Peter Keegan, an Irish priest who sympathizes with the British. Along with You Never Can Tell and Captain Brassbound's Conversion, which were included in the collections Plays Pleasant and Plays for Puritans, he wrote about Andrew Undershaft's rocky relationship with his daughter, the titular Salvation Army officer. This Irish-born playwright of Misalliance, Saint Joan, The Doctor's Dilemma, Arms and the Man, Major Barbara, and Pygmalion.

A word in the first line of this poem is a reference to author's theory of history described in the philosophical text A Vision. First printed in "The Dial," it references a blood-dimmed tide which drowns a ceremony of innocence, a lion's body with the head of a man, and a rough beast wakened after two thousand years of stony sleep. Also lamenting that "the falcon cannot hear the falconer" and presenting the theory of the "widening gyre," this poem was the source of the title for the book Things Fall Apart. Name this poem by William Butler Yeats named for the prophesied return of Jesus?

In one of this writer's 2007 works, Detective Landsman is summoned by his landlord to investigate the murder of Mendel Shpilman, the son of the local mafia boss who had the ability to perform miracles. Another 2007 work paired the horsethieves Amram and Zelikman in the area of modern day Azerbaijan. This author is perhaps better known for his first two novels, which are set in Pittsburgh, and his third novel, which follows cousins who create the comic book The Escapist. Name this author of Gentlemen of the Road, The Yiddish Policemen's Union, The Mysteries of Pittsburgh, Wonder Boys, and The Amazing Adventures of Kavalier & Clay.

His music for the radio play The City Wears a Slouch Hat was written entirely for percussion, while another work portrayed the tendency towards tranquility found in Indian aesthetic thought. His most notable collection of writings, dedicated "To Whom it May Concern", includes a section in which he heard a high-pitched whine in a soundless room, while the notes of his Music for Piano were determined by imperfections in the staff paper. This composer of Sonatas and Interludes wrote a work for twelve radios but may be best known for a three-movement work for solo piano in which the sections are delineated by a stopwatch. Identify this author of Silence who used the I Ching to introduce chance effects into compositions such as Imaginary Landscape and Music of Changes but may be best known for his entirely silent 4'33".

This author created the swindling notary Roguin in a novel about a man who gives up his Legion of Honor ribbon during a bankruptcy. A mysterious "Eureka!" is the last word of Balthazar Claes, the main character of this man's novel The Quest for the Absolute. A magic, wish-granting preserved animal product shrinks every time Raphael Valentin uses it in this man's novel The Wild Ass's Skin. His autobiographical Louis Lambert was included in the "Philosophical Etudes" section of a work that also includes the groups "Scenes from Parisian Life" and "Scenes from Country Life." name this author of Eugénie Grandet and Le Père Goriot, parts of his cycle The Human Comedy.

One of this man's religious poems is divided into the sections "Exposition," "The World," and "The Devil," and he wrote a play whose main character is a soccer player who smokes constantly and never talks. In addition to "Ode to the Most Holy Eucharist" and When Five Years Pass, he wrote a play in which a scorpion threatens the love of Sylvia and Boybeetle, who is also being tempted by the titular enchantment. This author of The Shoemaker's Prodigious Wife and The Butterfly's Evil Spell also described Leonardo's mutually fatal duel with the Bridegroom in the first play of his Rural Trilogy. Name this author of Blood Wedding and The House of Bernarda Alba.

In one story by this author, the umbrella-maker's daughter accuses a character taken in by Simeon, the saintly Lorenzo, of being the illicit father of a bastard child, but Lorenzo dies in a fire and is discovered to be a woman. In another story by this man, thousands of other sinners attempt to follow Kandata, who is using the title object to escape from Hell. In addition to "The Martyr" and "The Spider's Thread," he wrote about Goi, who receives a ludicrous amount of his favorite food in "Yam Gruel," and about a woman who steals hair from the dead to make wigs at the titular gate in Kyoto. Name this author of "Rashomon" and "In a Grove."

In this novel, a man becomes agitated when he recognizes the handwriting on an anonymous valentine, and later, the main character erases part of a message written on a coffin lid that reveals a pregnancy. A man who was thought lost at sea returns just before he is to be declared dead, but is shot near the end of the novel by William Boldwood. The protagonist must work at Weatherbury Farm after his dog chases all of his sheep over a cliff, which occurrs shortly before Sergeant Troy's attempt to elope with Fanny Robin is thwarted when Fanny goes to the wrong church. Name this novel in which Gabriel Oak finally does marry Bathsheba Everdene, written by Thomas Hardy.

This man becomes involved in a scheme to train an eagle named Caligula to hunt iguanas, after making a living through stealing books and running illegal immigrants from Canada. He aids in Mimi Villars's abortion after learning his wily ways from Grandma Lausch, and he later serves on the Sam McManus, which is torpedoed, as a Merchant Marine. In Acatla, he attempts to save Leon Trotsky's life, and he ultimately marries Stella Chesney after a long affair with Thea Fenchel. Name this man who opens his narration by stating "I am an American, Chicago-born," the title character of a Saul Bellow novel about his "adventures."

In one of this author's stories, Joe buys molasses candy for his wife with a fake gold coin, which was earlier used by the ice-cream man Otis Slemmons to seduce Joe's wife Missie May Banks. Besides "The Gilded Six-Bits," this author wrote about Jim Meserve raping Arvay Hensen Meserve under a sacred mulberry tree in one book. The protagonist of another novel divorces Lucy and remarries Hattie Tyson, which leads to a scandal that costs John Pearson his job as a preacher at Zion Hope. In addition to Seraph on the Suwannee and Jonah's Gourd Vine, in she wrote a novel in wich a rabid dog bites Tea Cake, forcing the protagonist to shoot him, after moving in with Joe Starks in Eatonville. Name this African-American author, who wrote about Janie in Their Eyes Were Watching God.

In one of this author's novels Persio intermittently offers monologues while observing the other passengers who were forced to board the insidious ship the Malcolm after winning a mysterious government lottery. In addition to The Winners, he wrote about Isabel tricking the Kid into being eaten by the tiger which is allowed to roam the house freely in his story "Bestiary" and he also wrote about a man who visits the aquarium Jardin des Plantes everyday before he eventually transforms into the eponymous salamander in his work "Axolotl." This writer's best known novel begins with a "Table of Instructions" and features Babs & Ronald, Wong, Ossip Gregorovius, and La Maga as members of the Serpent Club along with Horacio Olivera. Name this Argentinean author who wrote Hopscotch and "Blow-up."

In one of these poems the speaker says "I sank and quailed / As if God's future thundered in my past" after reading "My Letters! All dead paper, mute and white!", while in another one the speaker asserts "Nevermore... Shall [I] command / the uses of my soul, nor lift my hand / in the sunshine as before." In the first one the speaker is grabbed "backward by the hair" by a "mystic shape", who tells the speaker he is "Not Death, but Love", while that poem begins, "I thought once how Theocritus had sung / Of the sweet years". "To the level of everyday's / Most quiet need" and "to the depth and breadth and height / My soul can reach" are among the answers the speaker offers to the title question of this collection's best known poem, "How do I love thee? Let me count the ways". Name this collection of forty-four love sonnets written by Elizabeth Barrett Browning.

One novel by this man depicts the siege of Casale and the wreck of Captain Wanderdrossel's ship, the Daphne. He collaborated with Richard Rorty and others on Interpretation and Overinterpretation, and he also wrote a study on the "middle ages" of James Joyce, The Aesthetics of Chaosmos. This author of The Island of the Day Before and The Mysterious Flame of Queen Loanna wrote a novel in which Inspector de Angelis and the Brazlian mistress Amparo both interact with a man who is trying to locate his friend Jacopo Belbo. Name this writer who described the conspiracy theorist Casaubon in Foucalt's Pendulum and the medieval detective William of Baskerville in The Name of the Rose.

One of this poet's works begins by asking Miranda to "Take this slave of music," and is entitled "To a Lady, With a Guitar," while he lamented that "love should be a blight and snare" in his poem "The Revolt of Islam." This poet described "The Spirit of Solitude" in his poem about the titular Last Man, Alastor. He noted that "the everlasting universe of things flows through the mind" in "Mont Blanc," while in a better known poem, this poet asked the "most musical of mourners" to "weep anew." Those lines come from this poet's elegy for John Keats, "Adonais", and he asked "If Winter Comes, can Spring be far behind?" in a poem written to "the breath of Autumn's being." identify this poet who wrote "Ode to the West Wind" and described a crumbling monument in his "Ozymandias."

Transactions in his movie include one in which a store owner buys the gun of a would-be robber for $250 and another in which the protagonist loses $1700, after which his girlfriend claims that "winning or losing is all one organic globule, from which one extracts what one needs." The protagonist claims that his mother is "too drunk to be an astronaut" while he and his girlfriend are being hunted down by the Stucci brothers. That girlfriend claims that Babe Ruth was the NBA's leading rebounder shortly before the climax of this film, in which the main character agrees to a game involving The King and Duck Johnson. Billy Hoyle claims to be "in the zone" during a competition in which he wins his share of a $5,000 purse, which loses to Sidney Dean attempting to disprove the title assertion. Identify this movie starring Woody Harrelson as a hustling basketballer who is himself hustled by Wesley Snipes.

This work includes "paired butterflies" that are "already yellow with August" and which hurt the speaker, and also notes "different mosses / Too deep to clear them away!" The speaker asks why he should climb the lookout, and stopped scowling at fifteen because "I desired my dust to be mingled with yours / Forever and forever and forever." The speaker also "played about the front gate, pulling flowers" while his hair "was still cut straight across [his] forehead." The narrator "never looked at the wall," and "never looked back" after being "called to, a thousand times." Ending with the speaker offering to meet the title figure "as far as Cho-fu-Sa," identify this poem concerning a spouse, an Ezra Pound translation of a poem by Li Po.

This man wrote the incidental music for the plays The Blind Heart and The Loves of Inez. He also created a Harpsichord Concerto for Wanda Landowska, and nearly simultaneously, a ballet for puppets entitled Master Peter's Puppet Show. One of this composer's works is divided into the movements Distant Dance, In the Generalife, and one that depicts the gardens of Cordoba, and is entitled Nights in the Gardens of Spain. This composer also wrote a ballet that included the Ritual Fire Dance and the song Will O'the Wisp, and his best known work uses cante-jondo singing and depicts a magistrate trying to seduce a miller's wife. Identify this man who wrote the ballets Love, the Magician and The Three Cornered Hat, a Spanish composer.

One work by this author features a figure whose poetry was criticised in the Rowdy-Dow and is an autobiography of the late editor of the "Goosetherumfoodle." Another of his title figures spends the entire story telling the narrator that he's dead, and was notable for writingthe "Bibliotheca Forensica" and translating into Polish "Gargantua and Pantagruel." One of his stories that opens with a quote from Seneca opens in a library at Number 33 Rue Dunot, Fauborg, St. Germain, while the protagonist notices a scythe and three spades in a boat he is about to use and the narrator presumes Legrand would call the title creature scarabaeus caput hominis. The creator of Fortunato and Prince Prospero, identify this author of "The Premature Burial" and "The Mystery of Marie Roget," as well as "The Purloined Letter" and "The Raven."

In one of his novels, the protagonist fled from "buffaloes," but later returned and helped create a "field of fire." The protagonist asks his wife if she is pleased with receiving an umbrella, two books and a chocolate piano for Christmas in his story "And There Was the Evening and the Morning," and he also wrote of a veteran who convinced a bureaucrat the title body part cost the government thousands in "My Expensive Leg." In a novel by this author, the protagonist's mother vows to kill the leader of the "blue-tunics," Ben Wackes, and her husband has breakfast every day at the Café Kroner. Identify this author of Billiards at Half-Past Nine.

One work by this author notes that it rejects the translation styles of Pound in regards to Li Po, who joins Tu Fu and Wang Wei in the title of the translated collection Three Chinese Poets. The sections "Meditations of the Heart" and "Romantic Residues" are found in another collection whose titular poem notes "the whole world shares your tears," All You Who Sleep Tonight. This creator of lonely violinist Michael Holme wrote of the iguana Arnold Schwartzenegger and cat Charlemagne in a work charting the relationship between John and Liz in Onegin stanzas and set in San Francisco. Besides authoring An Equal Music and Golden Gate, he wrote of Rupa Mehra's attempts to secure the titular individual for her daughter Lata in his best-known work. Identify this Indian writer noted for the ginormously large novel A Suitable Boy.

Interestingly, in one interview Tom Stoppard called this play "the first tragicomedy." A study in the extremism of integrity, it juxtaposes the hero's hatred of artificiality against his love interest's wanton superficiality. The pair find comic foils in their manservants - Du Bois and the Basque - and serious ones their friends, the rationalist, middle-of-the-road couple Philinte and Éliante. The plot revolves around the hero's disgust with the woman pursuing him, Arsinoé, as well as Acaste, Clitandre, and the other suitors of Célimène. Most notable of these is Oronte, who writes her an abysmal love sonnet and brings the hero up on slander charges when he criticizes it. That hero, Alceste, eventually wins Célimène's love but is too disgusted with humanity to marry her and goes into exile. For 10 points identify this 1666 "comedy" by Molière.

One subplot in this novel is octogenarian Brigadier General Pudding's illicit passion for being defecated on by a woman dressed up as Lady Death; another concerns the medium Carroll Eventyr's astral quest to learn about a seraph who appeared in the sky fighting Luftwaffe with a flaming sword. The Soviet Purkyevitch trades the pedophilic Pavlovian Dr. Pointsman a giant semi- intelligent octopus named Grigori. Major figures include Katja, a Dutch Resistance fighter who nevertheless sold Jews to the SS and wants redemption, and American statistician Roger Mexico who longs to find meaning in the Poisson Distribution. Its hero is Tyrone Slothrop, who somehow predicts rocket trajectories by getting an erection. For 10 points identify this 1973 novel which famously begins "A screaming comes across the sky," a work of Thomas Pynchon.

In one of this author's poems, a woman makes a tentative peace with evanescence, deciding that "Death is the mother of beauty, mystical." This author's daughter Holly regards that poem as this author's greatest work, and this author also wrote, in the same poem, "Complacencies of the peignoir, and late/ Coffee…And the green freedom of a cockatoo/ Upon a rug mingle to dissipate/ The holy hush of ancient sacrifice." This author of "Sunday Morning" and "Anecdote of the Jar" also wrote of whipping "concupiscient curds" in "kitchen cups" by "the roller of big cigars." name this poet of the collection Harmonium and the poem "The Emperor of Ice-Cream."

The protagonist of this novel is visited by her sister-in-law, the Countess Gemini, who tells her stories of her husband's past, and other characters in this novel include Mr. Bantling. The protagonist's father dies at the beginning of the novel, and her aunt takes her to London to live at Gardencourt. The protagonist visits London with Henrietta Stackpole and her cousin Ralph Touchett, and she rejects marriage proposals from Lord Warburton and Caspar Goodwood. The protagonist is married to a man whose affair with Madame Merle produced the child Pansy, Gilbert Osmond. Name this novel about Isabel Archer, written by Henry James.

In one work by this author, the king's brother admires the wife of the title character, and despite her refusals Don Gutierre del Solis has her killed. Another features Curcio mortally wounding his son Eusebio. In addition to The Physician of his Honor and The Devotion of the Cross, another work by this man features Clotaldo and the Polish king Basilio, who locks his son in a tower after a prophecy reveals that the son would one day take the father's throne. In addition to that play about Prince Segismund, he wrote a play in which Philip II appoints Pedro Crespo to the titular government position. Name this Spanish playwright of Life is a Dream and The Mayor of Zalamea.

One character in this novel falls in love with Morten Schartzkopf when she goes to the seashore to avoid the man who would become her first husband, but marries that man due to her family's wishes. She would later divorce that man, Herr Grunlich and marry Herr Permaneder, despite having a daughter, Erica, with Herr Grunlich. After the parents of the titular family, Jean and Frau, die, the children Christian, Antonie, and Tom fight over inheritance, and Tom's son Hanno dies during a typhoid epidemic, bringing an end to the family line. Name this novel about the decline of the titular merchant family from Lubeck, a work of Thomas Mann.

Despite having never visited India, this man wrote "Sketches of India," which was one of his two wildly popular travelogues. Late in his life, this man wrote such literary redactions as "The Boy's Froissart," while his earlier works, like "Thar's More in the Man Than Thar Is In The Land," are characterized by a distinctive regional dialect. His only novel is entitled Tiger Lilies, about the wartime experiences of a soldier, and his more notable works include "Centennial Meditation" and "Sunrise," which is contained in his set Hymns of the Marshes, which also contains "The Marshes of Glynn." name this poet of the American South, who wrote "The Song of the Chattahoochee."

This author's works of translation influenced his novel which begins with the death of Gaspar Ilom, and deals with the conflict between the Indians, who consider themselves to be the titular figures, and those who merely grow corn. In one of this author's novels, Octavio Sansur attempts to organize a strike. That novel, The Eyes of the Interred, is the last in the "Banana Trilogy", which also includes Strong Wind and The Green Pope. Another novel by this author begins with the Zany killing Colonel Sonriente. Later, General Canales has a heart attack after reading that the titular figure was present at his daughter Camila's wedding and Angelface is arrested. Name this author of Men of Maize and El Senor Presidente.

In one of this man's works, he wrote that "dragonflies draw flame; as tumbled over rim in roundy wells." Homoerotic longing is expressed in such works of his as "Epithalamion" and "The Bugler's First Communion." In addition towriting "The May Magnificat" and "Heaven-Haven," this man coined the term "twindles" to express a combination of twine and dwindles, in his poem "Inversnaid." Religion inspired him to write a poem memorializing some nuns, "The Wreck of the Deutschland" and some of his other poetry includes "Pied Beauty," "Carrion Comfort," and "As Kingfishers Catch Fire." name this Victorian poet, author of "The Windhover" and user of sprung rhythm.

In this work's second book, the author states that "With music one can seduce men to every error and every truth: who could refute a tone?" in section 106, titled "Music as advocate." Its prelude includes such lines as "smooth ice is nice for those who dance with expertise" and "like the flame, unquenched, unsated, I consume myself and glow" among 63 rhymes, the penultimate of which is titled after another of the author's books. In one of its most famous sections, the author discusses how society has yet to overcome an immense shadow on the wall of a cave, and he also brings up a demon who reveals that life is to be lived over again eternally, foreshadowing a topic in Thus Spoke Zarathustra. Name this work by Friedrich Nietzsche which asserts that "God is dead."

This author described the town of Eriecreek as "mortally dull, narrow, and uncongenial" as the hometown of Kitty who takes up with Arbuton, a personification of Boston, in A Chance Acquaintance. Some consider his character of Squire Gaylord to be modeled on Mark Twain, although probably not the part where he walks out on his wife Marcia, who then finds solace in the arms of Ben Halleck. In addition to the novel about divorce A Modern Instance, he is best known for a work in which Tom Corey falls in love with Penelope, who along with Irene, are heiresses of a paint fortune. Name this author of The Rise of Silas Lapham.

One of these poems asks Esau not to plant himself in the speaker's heart because the speaker grows too quickly. This evokes the first, which describes a growing tree that ushered in a silence where everything was new in an auditory temple. The fifth states that the title character is present whenever there is song, that the bars of the Lyre are no prison to him, and that no memorial should be built for him. The eighth of the second section mentions a child who sometimes steps under the falling ball and is in memoriam of the author's cousin Egon, who died in childhood. Written after the death of and dedicated to Vera Knoop, a playmate of his daughter, name this collection of Rilke addressed to the Thracian king who invented the lyre.

He delivered a series of lectures on the political system of Greece and the role of technology in society as reflected in a poem about the Danube. In 1926 he was visited by a man whom he criticized for having a lack of historical understanding and prioritizing theoretical knowing. That former teacher was later removed from the dedication page of his masterwork upon the suggestion of Niemeyer. His former lover called his treatment of Husserl tantamount to homicide as he, acting as Rector of Freiburg University, expelled academics of Jewish descent. Name this German philosopher and Nazi collaborator, proponent of the concept of Dasein, and author of Being and Time.

One of his poems mentions a "hated poet" who, after realizing that success and poetry are mutually exclusive, threw himself in a river in 278 BC. Another poem discusses the moon shining bright on a southern port city, his two children alone and not knowing why his wife is crying over his absence. His poem "Gazing at Spring" is recalled by a haiku about Yoshitsune's final defeat by Basho, as both note that rivers and hills remain where there was once a great battle. The author of "The Ballad of the Army Carts," his life was disrupted by the An Lushan rebellion, and legend states that he died after overindulgence of food and wine after a ten day fast. For 10 points name this younger of the two great Tang poets who wrote many poems addressed to Li Bai.

This work closes with lines from Friedrich Ruckert's translation of Hariri's Makamen, as consolation for those unhappy with the faulting progress of science. Michael Poizat in The Angel's Cry offers that this work's titular analysis can help to explain why people would stand outdoors for more than a dozen hours to watch a performance of Tristan and Isolde. The author argues that only the traumatic, specifically war. Genuinely contradicts the title concept. The author asserts that due to the primality of the inanimate over the animate, we conclude though acts of neurotic repetition that the goal of all life is death. Introducing "Thanatos" or the death instinct as a modification to a previous conceptual framework, name this 1920 work of psychology, representing a major theoretical shift in the thought of its author Sigmund Freud.

Ralph Waldo Emerson in Parnassus, offers that this poem is about the death of a poet and his poetical mistress, but suggests a prize be given to an essay that explains its "frames and allusions." It describes the "mutual flame" of the two figures with a metaphysical conceit "Two distincts: divisions none/Number there in love was slain." This poem's preoccupation of the paradox of unity in duality is further illustrated by such lines as "Property was thus appaled/That the self was not the same/Neither two nor one was called." Historicized interpretations have offered that the title figures refer to either John and Ursula Salisbury or Queen Elizabeth and the Earl of Essex. First published in a collection edited by Robert Chester, Love's Martyr or Rosalins Complaint; it attributes "Single Nature's double name" to the two titular birds. Identify this poem by William Shakespeare.

In Dryden and Lee's version of this work, they add a sleep-walking scene which resembles the one in Macbeth. Hofmannsthal's version includes a second title character and thus shares its title with a painting by Ingres on the same theme. In addition to Gide's darkly comic existentialist version, Corneille's version of this play attempts to maintain the bienseance of his time by exonerating both kings of the killing of Laius. Cocteau's treatment of this play introduces the Egyptian god Anubis and the description "the bitch that sings" refers to the winged creature that is killing the people of Thebes and is titled The Infernal Machine. Name this Sophocles play wherein the title character blinds himself on the broaches of Jocasta's dress.

One of her novels focuses on the Place-du-Bois plantation and the life of its owner Thérèse Lafirme and she wrote of a discussion between the lawyer Paxton and Madame Célestin concerning her impending divorce. In one of her short stories, the presence of Alcée Laballière spurs Bobinot to meet Calixta at the titular event, and, in another work, Bobinot eventually gets some during the titular weather phenomenon. In addition to "At the 'Cadian Ball" and "The Storm", she wrote about the separation of Armand and his wife after it is revealed that she produced a black bay in "Désirée's Baby." name this author who wrote of Edna Pontellier's experiences with Creole culture on the Grand Isle in The Awakening.

This work ends with the "Uji Chapters," whose stylistic shifts have led some to speculate a second author. Previous sections include "Vanished Into the Clouds" and "Illusion," and the title character of this work has a name that roughly translates as "Purple." Taking place fifty years before it was written, the work is made up of almost 800 embedded poems called "wakas." Written by a member of the imperial court, it takes place in the Heian period. What is this novel, often considered the world's first, written by Murasaki Shikibu?

This poem describes spheres moving "far out in space/ Where our telescopes cannot reach" to describe the turning of the wheels in the "world clock," and toward its close it predicts "Delivery from the tyrants' chains/ Generosity also toward the villain," and "Mercy from the final judge." It thrice addresses the "millions," telling them to "endure courageously" and give "this kiss to all the world," though it also suggests that anyone who has failed to find a true friend should "creep/ Tearfully away from this band." In its first verse, it claims that "drunk with fire we enter" its title entity's "heavenly sanctuary," and calls that title entity the "beautiful spark of the gods/Daughter of Elysium." name this poem by Friedrich Schiller about universal happiness and brotherhood.

This word was anagrammatized in a song by Ottawan, and a Metro Station song describes a girl who is dying on the floor of one. Moxy Fruvous added this word to modify their "Video Bargainville" in the "c" album, and in Steve Martin's "King Tut," this word is applied to Tut before the line, "The ladies love his style." This type of "lady" is told to "shake it up, shake it down" in a song by Johnnie Taylor, and it is also the first word of the title of the only hit by Rick Dees. A band whose name ends with this word recently released Pretty. Odd and is most famous for "I Write Sins not Tragedies." Applied to "Inferno"s in songs by The Trammps and 50 Cent, name, this much-despised late-1970s genre of dance music.

One character in this play notes that, in his day, everyone either became a doctor, a lawyer, or worked in a shop, and later notes that once the star of one's honesty goes out, it can never relight. Its minor characters include Frank, who was always a year older than the drafting age and constructs an astrology chart for Larry, as well as the boy Bert, who arrives occasionally to ask for the keys to the jail. It begins as a storm blows over the tree in the backyard that commemorates an MIA pilot and brother of Chris, which foretells the arrival of his sweetheart Ann Deaver, the daughter of a man who remains in jail for his part in profiteering. Name this play where Joe Keller realizes that the soldiers killed by his faulty parts belong to the title group, by Arthur Miller.

Dollie Urquhart's father calls her by this name in a D.H. Lawrence short story, and W. Somerset Maughm wrote a children's story about one of them named September "and the Nightingale." Another title character who becomes one decides to go to a convent instead of marrying the Duke of Nemours after her husband's death; that character stars in a Madame de Lafayette novel set in Cleves. This word also describes Christina Light in the second novel in which she appears, after she has married Casamassima, and also describes a title inhabitant of Miss Minchin's boarding school, Sara Crewe, who is a "little" one in a Louisa Hodgson Burnett novel. Name this word that also describes a Hans Christian Anderson character who discerns the presence of a pea.

This novel includes a history of how an Ainu youth leads a group of farmers across the Shiokari Pass to settle Junitaki, written by a nameless, ancient Professor. Its protagonist names a cat Kipper at the urging of a chauffeur after being hired by operatives of The Boss to abandon his translating and restaurant reviewing to investigate the title entity. After being abandoned at the Dolphin Hotel by Kumiko, that protagonist returns to J's bar to mourn an event that took place in a mountaintop Hokkaido cabin, where the Rat suicidally defeated the monstrous title creature. Name this novel, followed by Dance, Dance, Dance, by Haruki Murakami, about a search for a mysterious woolen animal.

In this novel, one character's sister arrives with Carrie and convinces her brother to purchase some clothes for the protagonist and later Mrs. Millie asks another character to be her maid, which is met with a quick "hell no". That character, who knocks out two of Mary Agnes's teeth, learn that her lost children Olivia and Adam were adopted by Samuel and Corrine. Before moving to Tennessee, the protagonist of this work meets Daisy, the fifteen-year old wife of Alphonso, and falls in love with a blues singer first seen at the Lucky Star, Shug Avery. Telling the story of Sophia, Harpo, Nettie, and Celie, name this epistolary novel by Alice Walker.

One character in this novel pushes his pregnant girlfriend into the snow and offers two cartons of cigarettes to another character to trample her stomach. The protagonist's double date with one character sparks a flashback to Tenju Hermitage and the instant loss of arousal for that girl at a picnic at Kameyama Park. One character discusses the story of Nansen and the kitten and, along with Tsurukawa, serves as the protagonist's best friend but betrays him to Father Dozen, superior of the title location. Ending with the discarding of arsenic and a knife, name this novel about Mizoguchi burning down the title religious structure, a successful novel by Mishima Yukio.
The Temple of the Golden Pavilion

One character in this play sings about how the world would be different "Had Hippocrates, or Galen" "but known this secret." One character threatens another with public dissection if she fails to do everything backward, and later, one character leads Bonario behind a curtain to spy on his father. That character points one woman to the gondola where Lord Politic Would-Be is supposedly cavorting with a girl. The second scene of this work sees the introduction of a dwarf, Nano, along with Castrone and Androgyno, and Corvino's wife Celia is promised to the title character by his servant, Mosca. Name this Ben Jonson drama about a dude whose name evokes a fox.

Aizen Myo-o is the bodhisattva of this in Japanese tradition. In Slavic paganism, Siebog and Shiwa were the god and goddess of this. The Greek god Anteros was a god of one type of this. The Hindu god of this rides a parrot and was incinerated by the third eye of Shiva after shooting Shiva with an arrow. The Greek deity of this incited Glaucus's horses, caused the death of Hippolytus, and was worshipped at Syracuse under the name "Kallipygos." The Roman deity of this is married to Mulciber, the Roman form of Hephaestus. Kama is the god of what feeling, which is also associated with Aphrodite and Venus?

In one of this author's novels, the protagonist realizes who Alice Somerset is after reading the first chapter of Followed Home from the Flying Food Circus, and a woman obsessed with the phrase "Come hither boys, and become men" is attracted to Eddie. In addition to describing Maria in A Widow For One Year, he wrote of Siggy Javotnik's plan to empty the animals from the Heitzinger Zoo in Setting Free the Bears. Wilbur Larch provides abortions and runs an orphanage, and a wrestling coach writes The Pension Grillparzer, in two of his other novels. Name this author of The Cider House Rules, The World According to Garp, and A Prayer for Owen Meany.

In one of his short stories, Seikichi drugs a beautiful woman in order to inscribe a spider on her back, and in another work Sonoko and Watanuki participate in a love triangle centered on Mitsuko. Along with Quicksand, he penned a nonfiction text on aesthetic values called In Praise of Shadows. In one of his books, an engineer Westernizes his uneducated wife; which backfires when he falls under the complete control of that character, Naomi. Another of his works involves a search for a husband for Yukiko so that Taeko won't have sordid affairs and focuses on four siblings in Osaka. Identify this Japanese author of Some Prefer Nettles and The Makioka Sisters.

One of this author's characters, Boonyi Kaul, is seduced by the ambassador Maximilian Ophuls, who is later assassinated by an Afghani mujihadeen. He also described the formation of VTO by Ormus and Vina, who dies in an earthquake, in a novel narrated by Rai that takes its title from a U2 song that this man wrote the lyrics for. A man dreams of being ordered to kill Ayesha after ending his affair with Alleluia Cone in his novel about the actors Saladin Chamcha and Gibreel Farishta, and this author of Shalimar the Clown and The Ground Beneath her Feet also wrote of Saleem Sinai. Name this writer of The Satanic Verses and Midnight's Children.

Rome, Lourdes and Paris collectively name one series by this author, and in one of this man's novels, a woman is raped on a pile of rope in a shed at Requillart. That work eventually sees the protagonist kill Chaval with a piece of slate before his rescue from the bottom of a mineshaft. Pauline nearly marries the death-obsessed Lazare in his The Joy of Life. Other titles such as The Dram Shop and Nana appear in his Les Rougons-Macquarts. Aside from such longer works as the story of a coal mining strike, Germinal, this author addressed three handwriting experts and various military officials in a letter defending Dreyfus. Name this author of "J'accuse"

This sculptor has few confirmed extant works, and among his uncertain attributions is the graceful Lycian Apollo. This son of Cephisodotus the Elder depicted a young god as Sauroktonos, holding an arrow in preparation for killing a lizard, and a stain on the thigh of one sculpture is attributed to a besotted man attempting to copulate with the statue. A missing right arm may have dangled grapes in front of a child in one of his works, and his infamous sculpture modeled after Phryne is a life-sized nude female figure of the goddess of love. Identify the fourth-century BCE Athenian sculptor of Aphrodite of Knidos and Hermes with the Infant Dionysus.

This novel's protagonist compares himself to Tom Sawyer in the cave and claims he's still looking for an exit. He journeys to a gay bar run by his friend Kikuhiko, who had an affair with an American when he was younger. One character in this work is a radio producer who thinks of herself as a fairy godmother, and another is a diplomat who gives the protagonist a dictionary after their meeting. Another character owns a red MG and believes in a so- called "pluralistic universe", and gradually becomes enthralled by the protagonist's maps. Himiko eventually flees Africa in, what novel in which Bird must choose the fate of his disabled son, by Kenzaburo Oe?

"No sword drawn before James the First of England" could have made this character more frightened than when he is cut while being shaved, which occurs after the narrator asks him why a journey from Cape Horn took six months. Bearing with him the property of Alexandro Aranda, this character arrives at Santa Maria and meets Amasa Delano, whose offer of a cup of coffee he refuses since he is unable to leave the San Dominick. However, he later leaps onto the Bachelor's Delight to avoid his death, after which he tells his story about the conspirators Atufal and Babo. Name this ship-captain, whose death ends a Herman Melville story of the same name.

Cornelia Parker was authorized to add loops of string to this work in 2003, which Piers Butler later cut. One copy of this work was made for Edward Perry Warren, who placed it in the stables, and Carl Jacobsen commissioned one for the Ny Carlsberg Glyptopek. One figure's hand is on another figure's waist in this work, which depicts a scene in which the participants have just finished reading the story of Lancelot and Guenivere. Originally entitled "Francesca de Rimini" and slated to be a part of the creators' Gates of Hell, name this Rodin sculpture which shows a man and a woman embracing.

A group of strangers in a railway carriage discuss the enlistment of their sons in this author's short story "War." This author also wrote about the impromptu performance of Il Trovatore on Doctor Hinkfuss's stage and about a tragedy based on La Vela's fiancee's affair, in Tonight We Improvise and In Each His Own Way, respectively. The title character goes to Rome and poses as Adriano Meis after he is presumed dead in The Late Mattia Pascal, while he main character imagines that he is the title monarch in his Enrico IV. A play in which a family interrupts a stage manager while rehearsing a play is, what Italian author's Six Characters in Search of an Author?

The speaker of this work remembers Mrs. Porter and her daughter, who "wash their feet in soda water." In the same section the speaker mentions a woman undone by Richmond and Kew after being bored by Highbury. The speaker talks to the wife of Albert in a closing bar and urges the reader to "consider Phlebas, who was once handsome and tall as you," and asks "who is the third who walks always beside you?" Earlier in the work the speaker ponders the Unreal City and Madame Sosostris' "wicked pack of cards." name this poem, which ends with "Shantih shantih shantih" and begins with "April is the cruelest month," a work by T.S. Eliot.

Veronica leaves New Bethesda in this author's Valley Song. Gladys keeps a blank diary and Piet refuses to respond to Steve's accusation in one work by this author, while Miss Helen reunites with Elsa in another of his works. One title character of another work talks to Outa while the other concludes that "our life is dumb." Ethel Lange communicates with Zachariah, who shares the titular bond with Morris in another of his works. Besides Boesman and Lena and Blood Knot, he wrote a play in which Sam drops his trousers in response to the title character's offensive joke, after discussing a dance contest. Identify this South African playwright of Master Harold and the Boys.

Early in this work, the narrator darkly reflects on two women sitting in front of a door with "Ave! Old knitter of black wool. Morituri te salutant," before saying farewell to his aunt. At one point the narrator finds a painting of a blindfolded woman holding a torch, and the narrator is later intimidated by the silhouette of a sorcerer standing in front of a fire after finding the man whom he is seeking. Among the final scenes in the novel is the main character lying to a woman about her fiancé's last words, which are actually "The Horror!" name this novel about the journey of Marlow to find Kurtz in the jungle of Africa, a work by Joseph Conrad.

In one of this author's short stories, The Master of the Perfect Word encounters Han Fook, who sees his bride from a pear tree. In another work, Pierre, the son of Johann and Adel Vergurth, becomes ill. In addition to Klingsor's Last Summer, The Poet, Rosshalde and a novel about the youth of Emil Sinclair, Demian, he wrote a novel about Joseph Knecht assuming the title of Magister Ludi. In another of his novels, Govinda sees the world in the title character's smiling face, and in another Hermine is killed by Harry Haller. Identify this German author of The Glass-Bead Game, Siddhartha and Steppenwolf.

One character in this novel claims that marriage is like dancing: "men have the advantage of choice, women only the power of refusal." Another character has been seeing a poor soldier named Thomas, contrary to the general's wishes, even though her father is burdened by gambling debts. Mrs. Allen constantly talks about how she can afford nice gowns during an invitation of the protagonist to Bath. Isabella is abandoned by Captain Frederick after breaking off an engagement to James, while James's sister loses sleep upon reading Ann Radcliffe's Mysteries of Udolpho. FTP name this novel about the reconciliation of Henry Tilney to Catherine Morland, a spoof of the Gothic novel by Jane Austen.

He cuts back and forth between the husband and the assailants more and more quickly as a rescue takes place in his early work The Lonely Villa. A fake pistol is revealed to be a wrench held by the titular character in his The Lonedale Operator. Before his adaptation of Tosca was rejected, he was a hop picker who sold books in Kentucky, and wrote the play The Fool and the Girl. Contrasting between the rich and the poor in A Corner in Wheat, his Pippa Passes was the first film to be reviewed by the New York Times, and he also filmed an icy rescue in Way Down East, starring Lillian Gish. Name this director of Intolerance who chronicled the rise of the KKK in The Birth of A Nation.

One of the props in this play is a gun that shoots a parasol, though only the man pulling the trigger knows this and everyone else on stage thinks the gun is real. During a scuffle another character shouts "Violence! Violence!"; that character is later found to have been tearing the label off a bottle of alcohol while in the bathroom. Among the drunken revelations in this play is that one if not both of the New Carthage professors present at the party are impotent. Name this play in which Nick and Honey are witness to the dysfunctional couple George and Martha, written by Edward Albee.

One of his characters leaves her husband Andre Chazal to win support for her cause, though this life of Flora Tristan is parallel to that of her grandson Paul Gauguin. Another of his characters, Don Anselmo, builds a brothel that houses the young Bonificia. In addition to the aforementioned The Way to Paradise and The Green House, he chronicled a conflict between the Brazilian Army and a group of militant settlers in The War at the End of the World and intimated on his military training in The Time of the Hero. FTP name this Chilean novelist who described a friendship with radio producer Pedro Camancho and a relationship with Uncle Urquidi's wife in Aunt Julia and the Scriptwriter.

In one of his works, Alois Straubleder leads the police back to his house where the fugitive Ludwig Goetten is hiding. He worked for a statistics bureau while working on his first novel, and another of his novels reveals that Leni Pfeiffer was in love with a Russian POW. A member of the "rubble literature" school, he wrote The Safety Net and A Soldier's Legacy in addition to the aforementioned media satire about a woman arrested by police for sleeping with a bank robber, The Lost Honor of Katharina Blum. Author of The Train Was on Time and Group Portrait with Lady, for 10 points name this novelist who wrote of the Fahmel family's rebuilding of an abbey in Billiards at Half-Past Nine.

Her story appears after that of Dido in Bocaccio's On Famous Women, and she is the focal point of the bottom right panel of Ghiberti's Doors of Paradise. Assad falls in love with this woman in a Karl Goldmark opera, and she attempts to elope with the sculptor Adoniram in a Charles Gounod opera. In one legend, a visitor was relieved to find that this woman's legs were not those of a donkey but merely just hairy. Another story claims that she gave up her virginity for a drink of water, and from that union came Menelik I, from whom all future Emperors of Ethiopia claimed descent. Name this ruler who in First Kings visited and asked riddles to Solomon.

He has "nothing to look forward to with hope," and before encountering him, one character had been to Rowe's. He wants to team up again with Harold Wilson, with whom he had bickered four years ago, and though his brother is "rich, a somebody - director in the bank", he only wants to earn enough money "to at least buy tobacco with/So he won't have to beg and be beholden". This character has come to help Warren "ditch the meadow", though a discussion of the meaning of home follows from Mary 's earlier claim that this man "has come home to die". Name this man with given name Silas, whose death is the title action of a Robert Frost poem.

The narrator of this work and his girlfriend invent the term "discovering archetypes" as a euphemism for having sex and refer to their child as "The Thing". Another character, the co-founder of the School of Comparative Irrelevance, creates as an alter ego an amalgam of Conrad characters called Seven Seas Jim, and claims that you can differentiate lunatics from cretins, fools, and morons "by the fact that sooner or later [they] bring up the Templars". The Plan is set in motion by Colonel Ardenti, who shows a supposed Templar manuscript to Diotallevi, Belbo, and Casaubon. Name this Umberto Eco novel which begins near the titular scientific device.

A nonfiction work by this author describes "a portrait of a moment, no more, in the life of [a] beautiful, volcanic country". Another work by this author claims that "Realism can break a writer's heart", and in a discussion of a riot he notes, "Humiliate people long enough and a wildness bursts out of them". He published an essay-length pamphlet on The Wizard of Oz in addition to the aforementioned The Jaguar Smile and Shame, but may be better known for a work about the "Shah of Blah", Haroun and the Sea of Stories, and a work that begins with Saladin Chamcha and Gibreel Farishta falling out of an airplane. Name this author of The Satanic Verses.

One character in this play notes that she "never travel[s] without [her] diary" because "one should always have something sensational to read in the train". Another character notes that only vegetarians go without their dinner while fighting over some muffins, and attempts to explain the rules of "Bunburying" before telling his Aunt Augusta that he "killed Bunbury this afternoon". Confusion reigns when Cecily Cardew and Gwendolen Fairfax believe themselves to be engaged to the same man, who doesn't actually exist. Jack Worthing, left as a baby in a handbag at Victoria Station, is discovered to have the first name Gwendolen desires in a husband, in what Oscar Wilde play?

One of this man's poems notes that "Twenty men crossing a bridge/into a village/are twenty men crossing twenty bridges/into twenty villages", and another claims that the "mules that angels ride come slowing down/the blazing passes, from beyond the sun". In addition to "Metaphors of a Magnifico" and "Le Monocle de Mon Oncle", he admonishes the thin men of Haddam for not seeing as the title animal "walks around the feet of the women around [them]" and tells the reader to "Call the roller of big cigars" because "the only emperor" is the title character. Name this insurance salesman and American poet of "Thirteen Ways of Looking at a Blackbird" and "The Emperor of Ice Cream".

In one episode in this novel, a bird's wing is suggested as an organ of propulsion and not of manipulation, and the hoarding of milk and apples is suggested as a duty on the part of the brainworkers. Muriel the goat can read and Moses the raven tells stories of Sugarcandy Mountain, getting a daily beer ration. Although Frederick of Pinchfield destroyed the windmill, Clover and Boxer decide to work harder to rebuild it, while the pigs extract eggs from the hens to pay for their liquor. FTP name this novel about Snowball and Napoleon, a metaphor for Stalinist Russia, by George Orwell.

"Do not be carried away by all kinds of strange teaching" and "Obey your leaders and defer to them" are among the instructions given at the end of this work. In this book, the author lacks the "time to tell of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah…David and Samuel", other than that they "did not receive what had been promised". This book omits the customary introduction of the other epistles by its author, and claims that Jesus is a new priest "according to the order of Melchizedek", which is interpreted as an order replacing that of the Levites. Name this Pauline epistle to some generic Jews.

One writer from this country wrote of a man who fears "Master Eric" and insists on hanging a bailiff even after he finds out that said bailiff has seven living children. Another writer from this country told "An Immortal Story" and wrote of an old French chef's attempt to prepare the titular meal in "Babette's Feast". The medieval history of this country was written by Saxo Grammaticus. The best-known author from this country told of a character that tries to win a prince's love so as to gain an immortal soul, because otherwise after three hundred years she would turn into sea foam. Name this home country of Ludvig Holberg, Isak Dinesen, and Hans Christian Andersen.

He tells of a girl who refuses to marry her teacher after he seduces her in "The Answer Is No." He wrote a work in which Adham's son Qadri murders his brother Humam, as well as a related work featuring the Jesus-stand-in Rifaa and the Muhammed-like Qassem, who are found in a volume that ends with Gebalawi's death, Children of the Alley. A work about the family that includes Yasin as well as the patriarch's second wife Amina ends with the death of the merchant Ahmad and the joining of the Muslim Brotherhood by one of his grandchildren. FTP, name this author of the novels Palace Walk, Palace of Desire, and Sugar Street, which comprise the Cairo Trilogy.

One of his works discusses The Fox Wars and "Effects of the trading posts" in The Character and Influence of Indian Trade in Wisconsin. He stated "each age writes the history of the past anew with reference to the conditions uppermost in its own time" which helped shape the so-called "New History." His The United States: 1830-1850 was published posthumously, and late in life he advocated a move towards regionalism and away from individualism and believed that we would continue our spirit in the pursuit of science. FTP name this author who wrote "The Significance of History" and proposed that the USA's character derived from moving west in his Frontier thesis.

One of his heroines is the wife of the soldier in the Gibraltar campaign, William Booth, who is lusted after by Robert James, while he revised of his plays, Tom Thumb, to become The Tragedy of Tragedies. One of his works is about the robber who helps his friend Count La Ruse out of jail and who marries Laetitia Snap without knowing that she often hid her lovers in the closet. That work, Johnathan Wild the Great, is not as well known as this man's work featuring Parson Adams and Lady Booby, which was follow up to Shamela. His most famous character is the enemy of Master Blifil, and is raised by Squire Allworthy. FTP, name this author of Joseph Andrews and Tom Jones.

In one of his novels, Maurice Levasseur joins the army to escape financial problems before France loses the battle of Sedan. That novel, The Downfall, is more characteristic than his work set in Les Nouvelles Halles, Savage Paris. One of his works involves a woman who catches the interest of the banker Steiner as well as Count Muffat, while in another work, the central character marries Coupeau and becomes owner of a laundry business.
